paragraphs.en: Would you {BET} on the future of this man? He is 53 years old.Most of his adult life has been a losing {struggle} {against} {debt} and {misfortune} .A war {injury} has made his {left} hand stop {functioning} , and he has often been in {prison} . {Driven} by heaven-knows-what {motives} , he made a {resolution} to write a book.
paragraphs.cn: 你会 <u> 下赌注 </u> 在这个人的未来上吗？他53岁了，成年后的大部分时间都在 <u> 与债务 </u> 和 <u> 不幸 </u> 进行一场失败的 <u> 斗争 </u> 。战争中受的 <u> 伤 </u> 使他的 <u> 左 </u> 手失去了 <u> 功能 </u> ，并且他还经常入 <u> 狱 </u> 。在不知是什么 <u> 动机 </u> 的 <u> 驱使 </u> 下，他下定 <u> 决心 </u> 要写一本书。

paragraphs.en: The book turns out to be one that has {appealed} to the world for more than 350 years.That former {prisoner} was Cervantes, and the book was Don Quixote .And the story poses an interesting question: why do some people discover new {vitality} and creativity until the end of their days, while others go to seed long before?
paragraphs.cn: 事实证明，这本书350多年来一直 <u> 吸引 </u> 着全世界的读者。这位前 <u> 囚犯 </u> 就是塞万提斯，而这本书就是《堂吉诃德》。这个故事引出了一个有趣的问题：为什么有些人直到生命的尽头还能发现新的 <u> 活力 </u> 和创造力，而另一些人却早早地就萎靡不振了呢？

paragraphs.en: We've all known people who run out of {steam} before they reach life's halfway mark.I'm not talking about those who {fail} to get to the top.We can't all get there.I'm talking about people who have stopped learning or growing because they have {adopted} the fixed {attitudes} and {opinions} that all too often come with the passing years.
paragraphs.cn: 我们都知道，有些人还没到人生半程就丧失了 <u> 热情 </u> 。我并不是在说那些 <u> 没能 </u> 登上顶峰的人。我们不可能都做到这一点。我所说的是那些因为随着年龄的增长而 <u> 形成 </u> 了固定的 <u> 态度 </u> 和 <u> 观点 </u> ，从而停止学习和成长的人。

paragraphs.en: Most of us, in fact, {progressively} {narrow} the {variety} of our lives.We {succeed} in our {field} of {specialization} and then become {trapped} in it.Nothing surprises us.We lose our sense of wonder.But, if we are {willing} to learn, the {opportunities} are everywhere.
paragraphs.cn: 事实上，我们大多数人都在 <u> 逐渐缩小 </u> 自己生活的 <u> 多样性 </u> 。我们在自己的 <u> 专业领域取得成功 </u> ，然后便 <u> 受困 </u> 其中。没有什么能让我们感到惊讶。我们失去了好奇心。但是，如果我们 <u> 愿意 </u> 学习， <u> 机会 </u> 是无处不在的。

paragraphs.en: The things we learn in {maturity} {seldom} involve {information} and skills.We learn to {bear} with the things we can't change.We learn to avoid self-pity.We learn that however much we try to {please} , some people are never going to love us—an idea that {troubles} at first but is {eventually} {relaxing} .
paragraphs.cn: 我们 <u> 成年 </u> 后学到的东西 <u> 很少 </u> 涉及 <u> 信息 </u> 和技能。我们学会了 <u> 忍受 </u> 我们无法改变的事情。我们学会了不要自怜。我们学会了无论我们多么努力地 <u> 取悦 </u> 他人，有些人永远不会爱我们——这个想法起初 <u> 让人苦恼 </u> ，但 <u> 最终 </u> 会 <u> 让人释然 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: With high motivation and {enthusiasm} , we can keep on learning.Then we will know how important it is to have meaning in our life.However, we can achieve meaning only if we have made a commitment to something {larger} than our own little egos ( (自我) ), {whether} to loved ones, to {fellow} humans, to work, or to some {moral} concept.
paragraphs.cn: 怀着高度的积极性和 <u> 热情 </u> ，我们就能持续学习。然后，我们就会明白生活有意义是多么重要。然而，只有当我们投身于比渺小的自我 <u> 更宏大 </u> 的事情时，我们才能实现这份意义， <u> 无论 </u> 是对我们所爱的人、我们的 <u> 同 </u> 胞、工作，还是对某种 <u> 道德 </u> 观念。

paragraphs.en: Many of us equate ( (使等同) )“commitment” with such “caring” {occupations} as teaching and {nursing} .But doing any {ordinary} job as well as one can is in itself an {admirable} commitment.People who work toward such excellence whether they are driving a {truck} , or running a {shop} make the world better just by being the kind of people they are.They've learned life's most valuable {lesson} .
paragraphs.cn: 我们中的许多人认为“奉献”是教书和 <u> 护理 </u> 等“关怀”类的 <u> 职业 </u> 所要做的。但是，尽自己所能做好任何一份 <u> 普通 </u> 工作，本身就是一种 <u> 令人钦佩的 </u> 奉献。那些致力于追求卓越的人，无论是在开 <u> 卡车 </u> 还是在经营 <u> 商店 </u> ，都通过成为他们自己这样的人让世界变得更美好。他们已经学到了人生中最宝贵的 <u> 一课 </u> 。
